question: Does a registered directional boundary packet create a target-blind quotient-selective harmonic response without an imposed gate?

externally supplied zero-sum directional B-neighbor packet with formal amplitude epsilon
native edge stock-flow projection, not material force
physical_mapping: graphite packet preparation, registered orientation, dimensional time/energy/length, contact and complex loss OPEN
target_exposure: 21.8/38.2 degree signals and weak load trend known; no packet coefficient or scale fitted to them
fitted_choices: none; d1=(2,-1,-1), d2=(0,1,-1) are a fixed integer basis for the directional subspace, not a material fit
sources: prior graphite-endogenous-gate and native-gate-dynamics notes at base 59814ea16e94ac4048dc878ef99d23097ca63b9b

result: Externally prepared directional boundary amplitude activates all N7/13/19 at s1 with common matrix [[-12,4],[-12,-12]]. Linear-epsilon matrices agree through s7; N7-N13 first differs at s9 by [[1/630,-1/1890],[1/630,1/630]], N13-N19 at s13 by [[-73/16216200,73/48648600],[-73/16216200,-73/16216200]]. No physical drag or seven-cell selection.
